title: Emergency Escrow + SIEM Export Runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook describes the operational pattern for emergency (break-glass) secret escrow, scheduled rotation, RBAC v2 controls for secrets access, the audit-log schema required for compliance evidence, and the SIEM export mapping we use for centralized monitoring. It is intended for on-call SREs, security engineers, and platform owners.

Scope:
- Applies to all Vault-backed secrets (K/V v2, Transit keys, database credentials) managed by the security-and-compliance team or delegated to product teams.
- Covers emergency access flow, automated rotation cadence, audit event format, evidence collection automation, and SIEM export configuration.

High-level principles:
- Least privilege: RBAC v2 policies should grant the minimum path and operations required.
- Ephemeral access: Break-glass tokens must be short-lived and require a documented approval step.
- Observable by default: Every secrets operation generates an auditable event that is exported to SIEM and retained per retention policy.
- Automated evidence capture: Rotation events, approvals, and emergency access artifacts are collected automatically into the compliance bucket.

Roles & RBAC v2 model (summary):
- Roles: security-oncall, infra-admin, app-owner, ops-runner, audit-reader.
- Groups map to identity provider groups (okta: security-oncall, github-teams:infra-admin).
- Policies: fine-grained Vault policies per-engine and per-path (e.g., secret/data/prod/* read/write limited; transit/encrypt only for services).
- RBAC v2 features: use policy versioning (policy_v2) with explicit deny support for break-glass paths.

Emergency (Break-glass) Escrow flow:
1) Triggering conditions:
   - Critical incident causing production outage where normal credentials are unavailable.
   - Severe security incident requiring access to sealed or inaccessible keys when standard HSM/KMS paths fail.
2) Activation steps:
   - Pager duty: oncall acknowledges incident and opens JIRA-SEC-INC ticket. (Ticket must include "break-glass" tag.)
   - Request approval: at least two approvers from security-oncall and infra-admin must add an approval comment in the ticket: "Approve break-glass for <target> at <time>".
   - Generate ephemeral token: security oncall creates a one-time-use, time-limited token via the Vault emergency-escrow endpoint. Command example:
     - vault write auth/token/create policies=emergency-breakglass ttl=1h orphan=true display_name="breakglass-<INCID>-<user>"
   - Escrow record: the token and justification are written to the secure escrow store (encrypted S3 with MFA delete) by security automation. Manually, paste into the escrow UI only if automation is unavailable.
3) Access and actions:
   - Use token to fetch secret only for the narrow operation required. No bulk exfiltration.
   - Capture all console commands and API calls (see Evidence automation).
4) Post-incident remediation:
   - Immediately rotate any secrets used or potentially exposed (see rotation section).
   - Revoke the ephemeral token: vault token revoke <token> and mark ticket with evidence links.
   - 72-hour postmortem with security and infra leads required.

Rotation policy (recommended cadence):
- Service account keys: rotate every 30 days or after any break-glass event.
- Database credentials (machine): rotate every 90 days with automated credential handshake (update service config and restart rolling).
- Long-lived external API keys: migrate to short-lived tokens when possible; otherwise rotate every 180 days and document business justification.
- Transit keys (master encryption keys): rotate per key-rotation playbook (annual, with KMS key rotation policy).

Rotation automation checklist:
- Pre-rotation validation: smoke test to confirm existing credential revocation path is healthy.
- Automated staging run: rotate in staging and run the end-to-end smoke suite.
- Canary rollout: update 5% of hosts and monitor errors for 30 minutes.
- Full rollout: update remaining hosts with progressive throttling.
- Rollback plan: immediate rollback to previous versioned secret or rekey if failures exceed threshold.

Audit log schema (secrets-focused events):
We require a structured JSON audit event for every secrets operation. Fields:
- event_id: unique UUID
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- actor: identity (idp:okta:user_id or svc:github:bot)
- actor_groups: list of groups (okta groups or GitHub teams)
- action: one of [read, write, create, delete, revoke, generate-token, approve, rotate]
- target_path: vault path or logical target (e.g., secret/data/prod/db-creds)
- target_type: [kv, transit, aws-cred, db-cred, token]
- outcome: [success, failure, denied, expired]
- reason: free-text justification or error message
- request_id: correlation id passed through system
- ip_address: source ip of request (if available)
- ttl: token TTL when applicable
- approval_ticket: JIRA-SEC-INC id if approval was required
- evidence_refs: list of S3/GS links to captured shells, recordings, logs

Example (single-line JSON for SIEM ingestion):
{
  "event_id":"d9f7b3c2-7f1a-4cbb-a7e9-0d12e8a1f7a9",
  "timestamp":"2025-02-18T23:12:06Z",
  "actor":"okta:U12345",
  "actor_groups":["security-oncall","infra-admin"],
  "action":"generate-token",
  "target_path":"auth/token/create",
  "target_type":"token",
  "outcome":"success",
  "reason":"break-glass for INC-2025-011",
  "request_id":"req-87a3",
  "ip_address":"3.21.55.100",
  "ttl":"1h",
  "approval_ticket":"JIRA-SEC-INC-2025-011",
  "evidence_refs":["s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/INC-2025-011/session-20250218-2312.tgz"]
}

Evidence automation (collection & retention):
- Trigger points: token generate, secret read on break-glass path, secret rotation, policy change.
- Artifacts collected automatically:
  - API call traces (Vault audit device JSON lines)
  - Screen/session recordings (tshark/ttyrec for approved console sessions)
  - JIRA ticket snapshot and approval comments
  - Pull request links if any infra/config changes occurred
  - Diff of policy changes (git commit id)
- Storage: encrypted compliance bucket (S3 with server-side encryption + KMS, MFA-delete enabled). Evidence object naming: <INC>-<timestamp>-<artifact-type>.tgz
- Retention: default 2 years for break-glass evidence, 1 year for routine rotations, adjustable per legal hold.

SIEM export mapping (example for Splunk/Datadog):
- Source: Vault audit device writes structured JSON to object store; Filebeat/Fluentd pulls and forward to SIEM.
- Mapping: event_id -> trace_id, timestamp->@timestamp, actor->user.id, actor_groups->user.groups, action->vault.action, target_path->vault.path, outcome->event.outcome, evidence_refs->artifact.links
- Alerts to create:
  - Single read on break-glass path outside an active incident ticket -> high priority alert + page security-oncall.
  - Generate-token events without a matching approval_ticket -> critical.
  - >5 failed read attempts on a high-value path in 10 minutes -> medium-high.
  - Policy change on secret policy file without an approved PR -> high.

Integration config snippets (conceptual):
- Fluentd parser: parse JSON lines, add route: vault.secrets.* -> siem-index:secrets-events
- Splunk props: TRANSFORMS set to extract event_id, actor, target_path; source type: vault:audit:json
- Datadog: use logs pipelines to parse event, add facet for actor_groups and approval_ticket, and trigger monitors on missing approval_ticket for actions generate-token or rotate.

Operational playbook (quick steps for oncall):
- If you see an alert for unauthorized break-glass read:
  1) Pause manual changes.
  2) Correlate event with JIRA-SEC-INC and Slack incident channel.
  3) If none, escalate to security-oncall and create ticket, set incident severity.
  4) Revoke suspicious tokens and rotate affected secrets.
  5) Collect evidence via automation hooks (if automation failed, run manual archival script).

Audit & compliance checklist for rotation/break-glass events:
- [ ] JIRA-SEC-INC created and linked to evidence
- [ ] Two approvers recorded for break-glass
- [ ] Ephemeral token created with TTL <= 1h and revoked after use
- [ ] Rotation completed and smoke tests passed
- [ ] Audit events exported to SIEM and present in retention bucket
- [ ] Postmortem scheduled and attached to ticket

Change log (short):
- 2024-08-15: initial draft (Leah Kim)
- 2024-11-02: added RBAC v2 policy guidance and token examples (Ravi Menon)
- 2025-01-10: added SIEM mapping and alert rules (Aisha Patel)
- 2025-02-20: clarified evidence retention & added sample JSON event for ingestion (Marco Ruiz)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want automated ticket creation for every token generate event, or only for break-glass? (Tradeoffs between noise and traceability.)
- Confirm retention with legal for cross-border incidents (APAC region).
- Evaluate rotating TTLs for break-glass tokens to 30m for higher risk paths.

Notes for implementers:
- Use the existing vault audit device configured to emit JSON lines; avoid legacy syslog output for secrets events.
- Prefer using identity-aware token creation (token display_name contains incident and user id).
- Keep this runbook linked from Confluence page CONFLUENCE-SEC-4521 and required in onboard checklist for app-owners that manage secrets.

Contact:
- Security lead: Leah Kim <leah@redwood.com>
- Oncall rotation: see CONFLUENCE-SEC-ONCALL (linked)

End of document.
